subsystem: diagnostic and setup contrast event component
implementation: handwritten readable C; instruction execution belongs only to the independent native oracle

implemented_routines.name: fx_diagnostic_contrast_begin / fx_diagnostic_contrast_step
implemented_routines.scope: Host-owned retained value, normal4..29 and expanded0..31 limits, semantic token handoff, busy state, hardware contrast writes and AC completion

implemented_routines.name: contrast menu placement
implemented_routines.scope: Four ROM strings beginning11ce, font7, unconditional LCD sleep/clear, 8121 selection and display activation

implemented_routines.name: fx_diagnostic_contrast_draw_value
implemented_routines.scope: All256 value-byte caption quirks, supplied host text, font7 LCD y8 glyphs and8121 protocol

prepared_policy: Begin compares the nativeCCF4 entry throughCD1E before the ordinary key controller.
Step accepts an already delivered semantic token at nativeCD24 and returns at the nextCD1E or AC completionCD44.
The host composes WAIT with its nonblocking key controller; no CPU frame, instruction address or fake RAM text local is exported into production state.
Existing contrast values are retained rather than clamped; all incoming byte values are covered by native tests.

Whole RAM, MMIO and callbacks compare with only native CPU stack8d00..8ded excluded. Complete native key-controller events copy the nativeCD24 RAM checkpoint first; the contrast comparison excludes no numeric or annunciator workspace.
gaps: Physical keyboard, timer and interrupt scheduling remain with the host.
The complete diagnostic sequence and welcome/ordinary key controller are composed by their separate event components.
